objective: Make the just-bash /dev/null guard catch aliases of the device, not only its literal spellings, and make the docs state its real limits.
scope: Security finding 1 in /home/user/holyagent/.git/holyagent/reports/assignment-0mw9roekg-jryb.md: isDevice in packages/runtime/src/pi/bash/devices.ts compares the normalized string only, so `ln -s /dev /tmp/d; rm /tmp/d/null`, `mv x /tmp/d/null`, `/proc/self/root/dev/null`, `rm -rf /dev` and `mv /dev x` reach the host device through ReadWriteFs.

Optional code findings in /home/user/holyagent/.git/holyagent/reports/assignment-0mw9roe9z-xm39.md: `cp missing /dev/null` and `cp -r dir /dev/null` return 0 (devices.ts:74); `/dev/null/` counts as the device where the kernel gives ENOTDIR (devices.ts:30).
